steps.description:
Python has many libraries with useful functions that you can import for use. You can make the program pause for a duration using the sleep() command from the time library. The following shows an example of how you use it:

# you need to import the library time # put this at the top of your program import time

print("Going to wait") # indicate seconds as a float in time.sleep() time.sleep(3.5) print("3.5 seconds has passed")

Create a program to ask user to input a float representing the number of seconds to wait. Display "wait" and then run a sleep() command to wait for the number of seconds. After that, display "done". Observe how the program runs.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

5

10

0.5

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) Test your program with the examples below: Observe how long it takes for "done" to appear

Example 1 Input seconds: 5 wait done

Example 2 Input seconds: 10 wait done

Example 3 Input seconds: 0.5 wait done

Create a program to simulate the seconds of a digital clock. It will increase the second repeatedly starting from 0. Display it on the screen. Wait for 1 second after each display. Note that the second will reset to 0 after 59.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Output (Red Text - User Input) 0 1 2 3 ... 56 57 58 59 0 1 2 ... the program runs forever

Run the following codes: value = 001 print(value) Notice that only 1 will be displayed while the leading zeros are dropped.

In order to display leading zeros, you can use the built-in command zfill() by specifying the total number of characters. Below shows examples of how it can be used: value = 5 print( str(value).zfill(2) ) <-- displays "05", total 2 characters print( str(value).zfill(4) ) <-- displays "0005", total 4 characters Note that value is cast to string as zfill() works only with strings. If the total number of characters indicated is less than or equal to the characters in value, then value will be displayed without leading zero.

Create a program with variable value and assign 99 to it. The program will ask user to input an integer representing total number of characters to display. Display value with leading zeros. For example, if user input 4, then 0099 will be displayed.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

5

4

3

2

1

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input number of characters: 5 00099

Example 2 Input number of characters: 4 0099

Example 3 Input number of characters: 3 099

Example 4 Input number of characters: 2 99

Example 5 Input number of characters: 1 99

Create a program to simulate the seconds of a digital clock. The number will count repeatedly starting from 0. Display it in two-digit format on the screen. Wait for 1 second after each display.

Follow the test output display format.


Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

00 01 02 ... 57 58 59 00 01 02 ... the program runs forever

Create a program to simulate the seconds of a digital clock. The program will ask the user to enter the start second and it will run for 10 seconds. It will display in two-digit format on the screen as it counts. Wait for 1 second after each display.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

1

57

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter the start second: 1 01 02 03 04 05 06 07 08 09 10

Example 2 Enter the start second: 57 57 58 59 00 01 02 03 04 05 06

Create a program to simulate the minutes and seconds of digital clock. The program will ask the user to enter the start time in the format MM:SS. It will then repeatedly display the time and increase by 1 second each time with 1 second delay.

Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

00:57

59:57

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter the start time (MM:SS): 00:57 00:57 00:58 00:59 01:00 ... the program runs forever

Example 2 Enter the start time (MM:SS):59:57 59:57 59:58 59:59 00:00 00:01 … the program runs forever

Create a program to simulate a digital clock. The program will ask the user to enter the start time in the format HH:MM:SS. It will then repeatedly display the time and increase by 1 second each time with 1 second delay. Follow the test output display format.

Test Input

00:00:57

15:59:57

23:59:58

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Enter the start time (HH:MM:SS): 00:00:57 00:00:57 00:00:58 00:00:59 00:01:00 ... the program runs forever

Example 2 Enter the start time (HH:MM:SS):15:59:57 15:59:57 15:59:58 15:59:59 16:00:00 … the program runs forever

Example 3 Enter the start time (HH:MM:SS): 23:59:58 23:59:58 23:59:59 00:00:00 00:00:01 … the program runs forever
